meta.description: Unified Python interface to 40+ bioinformatics services. Use when querying multiple databases (UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, Reactome) in a single workflow with consistent API. Best for cross-database analysis, ID mapping across services. For quick single-database lookups use gget; for sequence/file manipulation use biopython.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabrication; accurately describes bioservices library access to 40+ bioinformatics web services with correct version warnings

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for multi-database bioinformatics queries; clear boundaries directing to gget for single lookups and biopython for file manipulation

methodological_ground.detail: Based on established bioinformatics databases and services (UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, NCBI BLAST) with proper API references

code_usability.detail: Code examples executable with proper imports; version compatibility warnings present for API changes

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of 40+ services with protein analysis, pathways, compounds, sequence analysis; version compatibility warnings for API changes; minor: some deprecated methods documented without full migration path

reliability.note: Good version tracking (1.16.0) with API migration warnings for UniProt and ChEMBL; NCBI email requirement documented; minor: error handling patterns not comprehensively covered

performance_context.note: Well-organized with clear sections for major service categories; reference files for detailed workflows; could benefit from rate limiting guidance

agent_usability.note: Excellent 'When to Use' with 9 specific scenarios; clear scope boundaries to gget and biopython; comprehensive examples; minor: trigger patterns could be more explicit

human_usability.note: Clear setup with Python version requirements (3.9-3.12), NCBI email environment variable, common workflow patterns documented

security.note: Proper credential handling with NCBI_EMAIL environment variable; openclaw metadata present; no hardcoded credentials; internet access requirement noted

maintainability.note: Excellent structure with version 1.3, license (GPLv3), upstream version tracking (1.16.0), API change warnings with migration dates

agent_specific.note: Strong composability with allowed-tools and openclaw metadata; cross-database workflow patterns; minor: output format specifications could be more standardized across services

key_strengths: Exceptional breadth covering 40+ bioinformatics services with unified Python interface
Excellent scope boundary documentation directing to gget for quick lookups and biopython for file manipulation
Strong version awareness with explicit API migration warnings for UniProt (1.10+) and ChEMBL (1.6.0+) changes
Clear cross-database workflow patterns showing real integration scenarios (KEGG → UniChem → ChEMBL)
Good security practices with NCBI_EMAIL environment variable and openclaw metadata for deployment

recommendations.title: Complete API migration paths for deprecated methods
recommendations.problem: UniChem API change warning present but new API usage not fully demonstrated
recommendations.root_cause: Version caveat mentions get_compound_id_from_kegg removal but replacement pattern incomplete
recommendations.fix: Add complete migration example showing old and new patterns side-by-side: old: u.get_compound_id_from_kegg('C11222'), new: res = u.get_compounds('C11222', source_type='kegg'); chembl_id = res['compounds'][0]['sources']['chembl']

recommendations.title: Add rate limiting guidance for web services
recommendations.problem: Multiple web service calls shown but no rate limiting or throttling guidance
recommendations.root_cause: Examples focus on individual calls without discussing bulk operations
recommendations.fix: Add best practices section covering rate limiting: NCBI 3 req/s, KEGG REST courtesy delays, batch operation patterns with time.sleep() or asyncio rate limiters

recommendations.title: Document error handling for multi-service pipelines
recommendations.problem: Cross-service workflows shown but error propagation not addressed
recommendations.root_cause: Examples assume all API calls succeed
recommendations.fix: Add error handling pattern: try/except blocks around each service call, graceful degradation when one service fails, logging for debugging multi-step workflows
